description: Registry of disclosed artifact-repository / package-registry compromises. Epyon's Layer 21 scanner cross-references target repositories against this list to flag references to known-compromised hosts and generate incident-response tasks. Add new entries as advisories are confirmed; never delete — mark resolved incidents with "status": "closed" instead.

incidents.description: Unauthenticated Artifactory authentication bypass allowed administrative repository access, enabling attackers to read or replace stored artifacts and access repository integrations between 2026-08-28 and 2026-09-15.
incidents.attack_path: Unauthenticated Artifactory authentication bypass -> administrative repository access -> read/replace stored artifacts and repository integrations -> potentially altered packages enter downstream builds and deployments.
remediation: Quarantine every artifact obtained from this host during the stated window.
Compare hashes, signatures and provenance with independently retained upstream releases; a matching package name or version alone is insufficient.
Rebuild critical software from reviewed source using clean, ephemeral workers.
Inventory deployments and containers derived from affected artifacts.
Rotate Artifactory tokens, build credentials and secrets reachable from the repository.
Retain suspect packages for analysis rather than deleting the only evidence.

notes: window_start/window_end are inclusive ISO8601 dates (UTC) bounding the confirmed compromise period.
Matches outside the window are still reported at reduced confidence since the scope of some incidents remains under investigation.
host matching is case-insensitive substring matching against URLs/hostnames found in package manager configs, container image references, and SBOM external references.
controls are NIST SP 800-53 identifiers for ATO/authorization-boundary impact analysis; they are informational only and are not evaluated against STIG checklists.
